title.narrative: Output 7.3. Increased capacity of member States to set adequate wages and promote decent working time

description.narrative:
In 2020, with the support of the ILO, the Job creation commission (JCC) implemented a job subsidy scheme targeting small and medium enterprises to address the negative impact of COVID-19.
In the framework of the policy responses to mitigate the impacts of the Covid-19 pandemic, the Ethiopian Job Creation Commission (JCC) has sought support from the ILO in September 2020 for the design of wage subsidies targeting small and medium enterprises. As the request was concerning more specifically the appropriate minimum wage level to be paid by the subsidised enterprises, the Office was able to share evidence gathered in the context of its ongoing support to the implementation of a wage policy in the country.
The ILO factsheet "Temporary wage subsidies" published in May 2020 also helped in providing assistance on this topic. These elements were discussed during a tripartite meeting early October 2020, where it was finally agreed to include in the scheme a commitment of enterprises to pay their employees at least 1850 Birr per month within the next two years.
Given the fact that female wage employees are more likely to be unskilled workers than their male counterpart (see https://www.ilo.org/africa/information-resources/publications/WCMS_728363/lang--en/index.htm), this minimum threshold is expected to have a greater impact on women and thus contribute to reduce the discrepancy between men and women in terms of pay.

Output 1.4. Strengthened social dialogue and labour relations laws, processes and institutions

description.narrative:
In 2021, 27 garment and textile factories have established joint worker-management OSH committees that are registered with Bureaus of Labour and Social Affairs. These committees are equipped with different tools to enhance OSH conditions through social dialogue by conducting self- diagnosis and risk assessment to ensure sustainable improvement. Regular (monthly) meetings conducted between management and worker representatives. The factories have now a system in place to record accidents and do regular report to the authorities.
A total of 34 garment and textile factories have developed grievance policies and procedures to resolve grievances at factory level. Through the trainings and the continuous advisory supports provided by the program, the factories are strengthened their grievance mechanisms to be more effective, and engaging workers in the process. Factories are giving more emphasis and creating attractive and secure grievance mechanisms to address cases of sexual harassment.
- One ILO Advancing Decent Work Program through the advisory service, supported 34 garment and textile factories to establish OSH committees. The capacity of the OSH committees are built to table and discuss OSH related issues in their respective workplace that fosters workplace dialogue; - Through the program, 65 participants (22 female) from garment and textile industry trained on workplace cooperation. The training brings together trade union members and management representatives. -Intercultural communication training is provided to 40 (15 female) local and expatriate participants from 10 factories with the view to understand the different cultures, increase tolerance and mutual understanding This training created an effective platform for the participants to address different intercultural and workplace communication issues in the factories.
-In collaboration with ITC/ILO, One ILO programme, developed grievance handling e-learning tool kit which is specially designed for garment and textile factories by taking into consideration their needs and contexts as well as the country laws. The learning tool is developed in English and Amharic to be more accessible to both local and expatriate staff. -A webinar on establishing effective grievance mechanism was organized for 20 garment and textile factories. The objective of the webinar was to enable managers and members of grievance committee to recognize the benefits of building an effective grievance mechanism at factory level, build their capacity to analyse the strengths and weaknesses of their existing systems and introduce new tools, polices and approaches to improve their system. -Through the continuous advisory services and follow up, the program is supporting factories to strengthen their grievance handling systems and polices to make them more functional and effective. -The program provided sexual harassment prevention training to 508 participants representing workers, supervisors and middle level
